entries.content_plain: 3-4. For what if some did not believe?-- It is the unbelief of the great body of the nation which the apostle points at; but as it sufficed for his argument to put the supposition thus gently, he uses this word "some" to soften prejudice. shall their unbelief make the faith of God-- or, "faithfulness of God." of none effect?-- "nullify," "invalidate" it.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16390"/><div sID="gen31789" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16390"/><hi type="bold">7-8. For if the truth of God, &c.--</hi>A further illustration of the same sentiment: that is, "Such reasoning amounts to this--which indeed we who preach salvation by free grace are slanderously accused of teaching--that the more evil we do, the more glory will redound to God; a damnable principle." (Thus the apostle, instead of refuting this principle, thinks it enough to hold it up to execration, as one that shocks the moral sense).<div eID="gen31789" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31790" type="x-p"/> On this brief section, Note (1) Mark the place here assigned to the Scriptures. In answer to the question, "What advantage hath the Jew?" or, "What profit is there of circumcision?" (<reference osisRef="Rom.3.1">Ro 3:1</reference>) those holding Romish views would undoubtedly have laid the stress upon the priesthood, as the glory of the Jewish economy. But in the apostle's esteem, "the oracles of God" were the jewel of the ancient Church (<reference osisRef="Rom.3.1">Ro 3:1</reference>, 2). (2) God's eternal purposes and man's free agency, as also the doctrine of salvation by grace and the unchanging obligations of God's law, have ever been subjected to the charge of inconsistency by those who will bow to no truth which their own reason cannot fathom. But amidst all the clouds and darkness which in this present state envelop the divine administration and many of the truths of the Bible, such broad and deep principles as are here laid down, and which shine in their own luster, will be found the sheet-anchor of our faith. "Let God be true, and every man a liar" (<reference osisRef="Rom.3.4">Ro 3:4</reference>); and as many advocates of salvation by grace as say, "Let us do evil that good may come," "their damnation is just" (<reference osisRef="Rom.3.8">Ro 3:8</reference>). <div eID="gen31790" type="x-p"/>

Therefore by the deeds of--</hi>obedience to<div eID="gen31808" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31809" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the law there shall no flesh be justified--</hi>that is, be held and treated as righteous; as is plain from the whole scope and strain of the argument.<div eID="gen31809" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31810" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in his sight--</hi>at His bar (<reference osisRef="Ps.143.2">Psa 143:2</reference>).<div eID="gen31810" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31811" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for by the law is the knowledge of sin--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Rom.4.15">Ro 4:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.7.7">Ro 7:7</reference>; and <reference osisRef="1John.3.4">1Jo 3:4</reference>).<div eID="gen31811" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31812" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Note, How broad and deep does the apostle in this section lay the foundations of his great doctrine of Justification by free grace--</hi>in the disorder of man's whole nature, the consequent universality of human guilt, the condemnation, by reason of the breach of divine law, of the whole world, and the impossibility of justification before God by obedience to that violated law! entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16400"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Rom.3.21-Rom.3.26">Ro 3:21-26</reference>. God's Justifying Righteousness through Faith in Jesus Christ, Alike Adapted to Our Necessities and Worthy of Himself.</title> <div sID="gen31813" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16400"/><hi type="bold">21-23. But now the righteousness of God--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Rom.1.17">Ro 1:17</reference>).<div eID="gen31813" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31814" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">without the law--</hi>that is, a righteousness to which our obedience to the law contributes nothing whatever (<reference osisRef="Rom.3.28">Ro 3:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.2.16">Ga 2:16</reference>).<div eID="gen31814" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31815" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">is manifested, being witnessed--</hi>attested.<div eID="gen31815" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31816" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">by the law and the prophets--</hi>the Old Testament Scriptures. Thus this justifying righteousness, though new, as only now fully disclosed, is an old righteousness, predicted and foreshadowed in the Old Testament. <div eID="gen31816" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: Ro 3:21-26 . God's Justifying Righteousness through Faith in Jesus Christ, Alike Adapted to Our Necessities and Worthy of Himself. 21-23. But now the righteousness of God-- (See on Ro 1:17 ). without the law-- that is, a righteousness to which our obedience to the law contributes nothing whatever ( Ro 3:28 ; Ga 2:16 ). is manifested, being witnessed-- attested. by the law and the prophets-- the Old Testament Scriptures. Thus this justifying righteousness, though new, as only now fully disclosed, is an old righteousness, predicted and foreshadowed in the Old Testament.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16404"/><div sID="gen31826" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16404"/><hi type="bold">25-26. Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation--</hi>or "propitiatory sacrifice."<div eID="gen31826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31827" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">through faith in his blood--</hi>Some of the best interpreters, observing that "faith upon" is the usual phrase in Greek, not "faith in" Christ, would place a "comma" after "faith," and understand the words as if written thus: "to be a propitiation, in His blood, through faith." But "faith in Christ" is used in <reference osisRef="Gal.3.26">Ga 3:26</reference> and <reference osisRef="Eph.1.15">Ep 1:15</reference>; and "faith in His blood" is the natural and appropriate meaning here.<div eID="gen31827" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31828" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to declare his righteousness for the remission--</hi>rather, "pretermission" or "passing by."<div eID="gen31828" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31829" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of sins--</hi>"the sins."<div eID="gen31829" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31830" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that are past--</hi>not the sins committed by the believer before he embraces Christ, but the sins committed under the old economy, before Christ came to "put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself."<div eID="gen31830" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31831" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">through the forbearance of God--</hi>God not remitting but only forbearing to punish them, or passing them by, until an adequate atonement for them should be made. In thus not imputing them, God was righteous, but He was not seen to be so; there was no "manifestation of His righteousness" in doing so under the ancient economy.
